Previous Week Recap
Buffett Steps Down As Chairman
: BRK.A: Warren Buffett steps down as chairman but stays on board; Greg Abel continues as operational leader; Susan Decker remains lead independent director. Premarket trading showed ~0.1% dip.
BRK.A Boosts Alphabet Exposure; Cuts Capital One
: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) boosted Alphabet exposure ~658% to become a top-three holding, cut Capital One stake 58%, opened a small D.R. Horton position and exited Constellation Brands.
BRK.A Cash Pile Near Record
: Berkshire Hathaway Class A (BRK.A) holds about $364.7 billion in cash and short-term assets, a near-record liquidity position available for future acquisitions and investments.
BRK.A Portfolio Tops $350B; No Overhaul
: BRK.A equity portfolio tops $350B. Management says no big overhaul; core stakes include Coca‑Cola, Apple, Moody’s. CEO Abel focusing more on operations than active portfolio shifts.
Greg Abel Becomes CEO Of BRK.A
: Greg Abel became CEO of Berkshire Hathaway Inc. Class A (BRK.A) at the start of 2026, replacing the prior CEO; Abel now leads the company relevant to BRK.A holders and traders.
Sold $15B From Todd Combs Sleeve
: Berkshire Hathaway Class A (BRK.A) sold about $15B of stocks from Todd Combs' former equity sleeve; Ted Weschler still manages roughly 6% and took on a smaller incremental role than expected.
Higher Rates Could Boost BRK.A Returns
: Higher short-term rates may boost BRK.A returns via rising T-bill yields, benefiting its large cash and short-duration holdings as analysts note potential Fed fund rate increases.
Abel Notes Kraft Heinz Consideration
: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) CEO designate Greg Abel said Berkshire considered selling its Kraft Heinz stake earlier; Kraft Heinz’s new leadership and turnaround efforts influenced Berkshire’s view.
Wescherman Cash; Howie Oversees Succession
: Ted Weschler will continue managing part of Berkshire Hathaway Class A (BRK.A) cash while Warren Buffett stays involved; Howie Buffett oversees succession to preserve Berkshire’s culture.
